definitions.explanation: Craft items made by hand rather than by machine. Encompasses a wide range of creative activities including knitting, weaving, pottery, leatherwork, and other manual arts.

examples.japanese: {手工芸|しゅこうげい}が{趣味|しゅみ}です。
{地元|じもと}の{手工芸|しゅこうげい}{品|ひん}をお{土産|みやげ}にした。
examples.english: I got local handicrafts as souvenirs.

examples.japanese: {手工芸|しゅこうげい}の{教室|きょうしつ}では、{編|あ}み{物|もの}や{刺繍|ししゅう}などを{学|まな}ぶことができる。
examples.english: In handicraft classes, you can learn knitting, embroidery, and more.

notes:
Composed of {手|しゅ} (hand) and {工芸|こうげい} (craft, applied art). Emphasizes the handmade quality of the work, in contrast to machine-produced goods.

USAGE:
Used both for the activity/hobby and for the resulting products. {手工芸|しゅこうげい}{品|ひん} refers to handcrafted items. Common in the context of hobby shops, craft classes, and artisan markets.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {手工芸|しゅこうげい}{品|ひん} — handicraft item, handmade goods
- {手工芸|しゅこうげい}{教室|きょうしつ} — handicraft class
- {手工芸|しゅこうげい}{作家|さっか} — handicraft artist
- {伝統|でんとう}{手工芸|しゅこうげい} — traditional handicraft

RELATED TERMS:
- {工芸|こうげい} — craft, applied art; broader term including machine-assisted work
- {民芸|みんげい} — folk craft; specifically traditional crafts of ordinary people
- {手芸|しゅげい} — needlework, sewing crafts; more specific to textile-based handwork
- ハンドメイド — handmade; the modern loanword, popular in online marketplaces
